basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 23.' and it opens '(Vers. 23.) Filii Aram, Us, et Ul, et Gether, et Mes. Us Trachonitidis et Damasci'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 23.) Filii Aram, Us, et Ul, et Gether, et Mes. Us Trachonitidis et Damasci conditor, inter Palaestinam et Coelen Syriam tenuit principatum: a quo Septuaginta Interpretes in libro Job, ubi in Hebraeo scribitur, terra Us, regionem Ausitidem, quasi Usitidem, transtulerunt. Ul, a quo Armenii: Gether, a quo Acarnanii, sive Carii. Porro Mes, pro quo Septuaginta Interpretes Mosoch dixerunt, nunc vocantur Maeones.
